task.swarm_objective: Produce a comparative analysis of NVIDIA and AMD's AI-related business performance, supported by financial filings and recent earnings information.
task.agent_directive: Research AI-related capital expenditure by Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta as a demand signal for NVIDIA and AMD, with cited figures.
constraints: Cite a source for every financial figure you record.
Use the most recently reported fiscal periods.
Focus on capital expenditure and data-center spending.

tool_arguments.query: Microsoft fiscal year 2026 Q2 capital expenditure AI data center spending

events.content: Microsoft fiscal year 2026 Q2 capital expenditure AI data center spending

Microsoft reported **$37.5 billion of capital expenditures in FY2026 Q2** (the quarter ended December 31, 2025), encompassing AI and broader cloud infrastructure investment. [[1]] 

About **two-thirds** of Q2 capex—approximately **$25 billion**—went to short-lived assets, principally GPUs and CPUs; the remaining roughly **$12.5 billion** funded long-lived infrastructure expected to support monetization for 15 years or more. [[1]] 

The data-center component also included **$6.7 billion of finance leases**, primarily for large data-center sites, while actual cash paid for PP&E was **$29.9 billion**. [[1]] 

Management said demand continued to exceed available supply, with investment directed at expanding Azure capacity, supporting first-party AI workloads such as Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot, increasing R&D compute allocations, and replacing end-of-life server and networking gear. [[1]] 

For FY2026 Q3, Microsoft initially guided capex to decline sequentially because of normal cloud-buildout variability and finance-lease delivery timing, while keeping the short-lived-asset mix similar to Q2. [[1]]

Sources:
[S1.1] Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call — https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/earnings-fy-2026-q2

source_references.title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call

tool_arguments.query: Alphabet fiscal year 2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

events.content: Alphabet fiscal year 2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

Alphabet’s **Q3 2025 capital expenditures were $24.0 billion**, with the vast majority directed to technical infrastructure supporting AI and cloud demand. [[1]] 

Alphabet allocated approximately **60%** of Q3 CapEx—about **$14.4 billion**—to servers, which includes AI compute infrastructure such as GPUs and Google’s TPUs. [[1]] 

Approximately **40%**—about **$9.6 billion**—went to data-center facilities and networking equipment. [[1]] 

Management said the buildout was driven by strong Cloud-customer demand and broader growth opportunities, while highlighting investments in NVIDIA GPUs and internally designed TPUs to expand AI infrastructure capacity. [[1]] 

At the time of the Q3 release on October 29, 2025, Alphabet raised its expected **full-year 2025 CapEx to $91 billion–$93 billion**, from its prior $85 billion outlook. [[1]] 

The higher infrastructure investment was already increasing earnings pressure: Q3 depreciation rose **$1.6 billion year over year to $5.6 billion**, or **41%**, and Alphabet expected depreciation growth to accelerate slightly in Q4, alongside higher data-center operating costs such as energy. [[1]] 

For context, Alphabet ultimately spent **$91.4 billion** in CapEx for full-year 2025; its later FY2026 plan called for **$175 billion–$185 billion**, illustrating the planned step-up in AI data-center investment. [[2]]

Sources:
[S2.1] Alphabet Investor Relations - 2025 Q3 Earnings Call — https://abc.xyz/investor/events/event-details/2025/2025-Q3-Earnings-Call-2025-4OI4Bac_Q9/default.aspx
[S2.2] Alphabet Investor Relations - 2025 Q4 Earnings Call — https://abc.xyz/investor/events/event-details/2026/2025-Q4-Earnings-Call-2026-Dr_C033hS6/default.aspx

source_references.title: Alphabet Investor Relations - 2025 Q3 Earnings Call
Alphabet Investor Relations - 2025 Q4 Earnings Call

tool_arguments.query: Amazon fiscal year 2025 Q4 capital expenditure AI data center spending

events.content: Amazon fiscal year 2025 Q4 capital expenditure AI data center spending

**Amazon FY2026 Q1 AI/data-center spending**

- Amazon’s Q1 FY2026 cash capital expenditure—reported as **purchases of property and equipment—was $44.203 billion**, versus **$25.019 billion** in Q1 FY2025, an increase of **$19.184 billion (76.7% year over year)**. [[1]]
- This is the appropriate reported capex measure for the quarter; it includes broad property-and-equipment spending rather than a separately disclosed “AI data-center” line item. [[1]]
- Amazon said its higher property-and-equipment investment **primarily reflected AI investments**, while its filings show that its relevant infrastructure footprint includes data-center facilities and server/networking equipment. [[2]] [[1]]
- The Q1 outlay represented about **22.1%** of Amazon’s previously stated plan to invest approximately **$200 billion in capex during FY2026**, spanning AI alongside chips, robotics, and low-Earth-orbit satellites. [[3]]
- On a trailing-12-month basis through March 31, 2026, purchases of property and equipment, net of sale proceeds and incentives, were **$147.299 billion**, up from **$87.978 billion** a year earlier; operating cash flow was **$148.531 billion**, leaving **$1.232 billion** in free cash flow. [[1]]
- Amazon therefore does **not** disclose a clean Q1 dollar amount solely for AI data centers; the defensible disclosed answer is **$44.2 billion total quarterly property-and-equipment capex**, with management attributing the overall step-up primarily to AI. [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S3.1] amzn-20260331 - Amazon.com, Inc. — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000014/amzn-20260331.htm
[S3.2] Amazon.com, Inc. - Amazon.com Announces First Quarter Results — https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-First-Quarter-Results/default.aspx
[S3.3] Amazon.com, Inc. - Amazon.com Announces Fourth Quarter Results — https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-Results/

tool_arguments.query: Meta fiscal year 2025 Q4 capital expenditure AI data center spending

events.content: Meta fiscal year 2025 Q4 capital expenditure AI data center spending

**Meta Platforms — Q1 FY2026 AI/data-center spending**

- Meta spent **$19.84 billion** of capital expenditures in Q1 2026 (three months ended March 31), including principal payments on finance leases; management attributed this to investments in **servers, data centers, and network infrastructure**. [[1]] [[2]]

- Following the quarter, Meta raised its FY2026 capex outlook to **$125–145 billion**, from **$115–135 billion** previously—an increase of **$10 billion at both ends** of the range. [[1]] [[3]]

- The revised outlook is primarily due to expected **higher component prices**—with management specifically highlighting memory pricing—and, secondarily, incremental **data-center costs** to create capacity for future years. [[3]] [[4]]

- Q1 operating expenses were **$33.4 billion, up 35% year over year**; infrastructure-cost growth reflected higher depreciation, data-center operating costs, and third-party cloud spending. [[3]]

- Meta characterized compute as strategically central to more capable AI models and new products, and said it is expanding its owned data-center footprint, securing component supply, and adding cloud capacity scheduled to come online during 2026 and 2027. [[3]]

- Those multiyear cloud arrangements and infrastructure purchase agreements produced a **$107 billion quarter-over-quarter increase in contractual commitments**, which is a commitment measure rather than Q1 cash capex. [[3]]

**Analyst read-through:** Meta’s Q1 result confirms a substantial acceleration in AI-infrastructure investment, but the FY2026 capex-guide increase was predominantly an **input-cost / component-inflation revision**, rather than solely a new demand-driven buildout; incremental future-capacity data-center spending was explicitly a lesser contributor. [[3]] [[4]]

Sources:
[S4.1] Meta - Meta Reports First Quarter 2026 Results — https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx
[S4.2] 1 Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) First Quarter 2026 Results Conference Call — https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/META-Q1-2026-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf
[S4.3] META Q1 2026 Prepared Remarks — https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/META-Q1-2026-Prepared-Remarks.pdf
[S4.4] Meta (META) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript - The Globe and Mail — https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/META/pressreleases/1604248/meta-meta-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript/
